conviction_note: Traffic data (Placer.ai fiscal-Q3 visits +7.2%, same-store +5.9%, vs ~+5% in Q2 when reported traffic was +3.6%) and a Street FY revenue/EPS sitting below the company's own guide point to a sales beat and a reiterate-or-raise; against that, a whisper 7% above consensus, a stock +89% off its 52w low, a +3.8 put skew, late-September price cuts and an October slowdown in both Placer and BofA card data. abs_move 7.0 (implied 8.27, own median 4.07), p_up 53, so the scaled number is +0.42 while the findings sum to -0.30: the findings say the margin/positioning negatives roughly offset the sales positive, the scaled number carries a slight lean that the fundamental read (a revenue beat) survives the high bar.
bar: Q3 consensus EPS $2.03, revenue $26.38B (+4.4% y/y from $25.27B), whisper EPS $2.17, Street FY EPS $8.43 and FY revenue ~$108.7B, all from Earnings Whispers 2026-11-10 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/TGT/23131, republished https://finviz.com/news/420701/...), effectively ONE estimate source; BofA's own Q3 model is comps +4%, EPS $2.08 (https://finimize.com/content/target-heads-into-q3-with-strong-sales-and-tighter-margins). Company guide (primary, https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/08/target-corporation-reports-second-quarter-earnings): FY net sales growth ~5%, FY adj EPS $9.90-10.90 incl. ~$1.65 Q2 tariff refund (underlying ~$8.25-9.25), FY op margin ~6% (ex-refund ~5.1%, +50bp y/y); no quarterly guide and no comp guide. Estimate bar single-sourced, so finding sizes are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 16.41M shares, ~3.61% of shares outstanding, 4.21 days to cover at the 2026-10-30 settlement, down from 17.26M (3.80%) on 2026-09-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/tgt/shortinterest, FINRA data, read 2026-11-17; Nov 13 settlement not yet published). Not a crowded short; no squeeze mechanism. Baseline skew_25d +3.81 vol pts (downside paid, moderate), put/call OI 1.0, implied event move 8.27%, ATM IV 105%. Tape: spot 158.34, run-up 20d +2.81%, 5d -2.13%, -6.8% off 52w high (~$170.7 on 2026-08-24), +89% off 52w low. EW says shares +12% since the Q2 report into 2026-11-10 and sentiment 'still bullish, somewhat cooler'.

findings.finding: Placer.ai (2026-11-11) puts Target's calendar-Q3 store visits at +7.2% y/y and same-store visits at +5.9% (October +5.0%), against Placer's Q2 figure of just under +5% that mapped to reported Q2 comparable traffic +3.6% and comps +3.8%; at the same mapping fiscal-Q3 comps land near 4.5-5.5% versus a consensus revenue bar of +4.4% total growth (Q2's +5.3% sales growth came on a 3.8% comp, so +4.4% implies roughly a 3% comp) and BofA's 4% comp model, i.e. roughly a 1-1.5% revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (2026-05-20): comps +5.6%, sales +6.7%, EPS $1.71 vs $1.41 consensus, sales guide raised to ~4% -> stock -3.86% on the day. Q2 2026 (2026-08-19): comps +3.8%, sales beat, guide raised -> traded down ~4% early, closed +4.28%. Sales beats on this name have been bought once and sold once in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The Placer article is public and a sell-side reader will have it, but the consensus revenue line ($26.38B, +4.4%) is BELOW Q2's +5.3% growth and below a Q3 traffic proxy that accelerated from Q2, while comparing against an easier year-ago comp (-2.7% in Q3 2025 vs -1.9% in Q2 2025). If it were priced, the revenue consensus would sit near +6% and BofA would not be modelling 4% comps; the whisper ($2.17) prices some of it on EPS, not visibly on revenue.
findings.independence: Same direction, different sources: Placer's October deal-days piece, Target visits +6.0% y/y on sale days (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/target-and-kohls-stand-out-in-octobers-deal-rush, 2026-10-19; same vendor, so partly shared); BofA card spending per household +6.2% y/y Sept, +5.8% Oct (https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-november-2026.html); Home Depot's Q3 (2026-11-17) comps +2.2% 'exceeded our expectations'. Proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: The Street sits below the company's own full-year guide: FY revenue consensus ~$108.7B vs a ~5% growth guide (~$110B), and FY EPS consensus $8.43 vs an underlying (ex-refund) guide of ~$8.25-9.25 (midpoint ~$8.75); with H1 underlying EPS of $4.17 ($1.71 + $2.46) the guide midpoint implies H2 ~$4.58 against the Street's ~$4.26, so a mere reiteration on Nov 18 implies Q4 above consensus, and a raise widens the gap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance moved up at both 2026 prints under the new CEO (May: sales to ~4% from ~2%, EPS to high end; August: sales to ~5%, underlying EPS midpoint +$0.75): -3.86% and +4.28%. Nov 2025 (old CEO, holiday outlook cut) -2.77%.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap between guide and Street means the Street is discounting management's H2, typically on holiday/home-apparel caution; if the market believed the guide, FY consensus would sit near $8.75 and ~$110B. The stock pulling back from ~$171 to ~$158 is consistent with that skepticism, so a reiteration or raise is not fully in the price.
findings.independence: Company guide from the primary Q2 release (https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/08/target-corporation-reports-second-quarter-earnings, 2026-08-19); H1 EPS from the Q1 release (https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/05/target-corporation-reports-first-quarter-earnings). Street FY numbers are single-sourced to Earnings Whispers; Earnings Whispers numbers also underlie finding 6 (whisper), so the two share a document.

findings.finding: Margin pressure inside the quarter: on 2026-09-29 Target cut prices on nearly 2,000 home and apparel items (selected apparel at least 20% below last year, bedding -15%, women's footwear $40->$35) with no stated financial impact, on top of SG&A that grew ~7% in Q2; BofA raised its Q3 comp to 4% but CUT its EPS to $2.08 on promotions, freight and SG&A, so an EPS print near consensus despite a sales beat is plausible against a $2.17 whisper.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin has been the swing line: Q2 2026 gross margin ex-refund +100bp drew a +4.28% close after an early -4%; Q1 2026 op margin 4.5% with a big EPS beat still closed -3.86%; Nov 2024 margin miss -21% (outside the 8-print baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper ($2.17) is 7% above consensus, so the market's informal bar assumes margin holds; if the price cuts and SG&A were priced, the whisper would sit at or below BofA's $2.08 and the stock would not be within ~7% of its high.
findings.independence: BofA analyst note via https://finimize.com/content/target-heads-into-q3-with-strong-sales-and-tighter-margins (EPS cut to $2.08, Underperform, $141 PO); Q2 SG&A +7% in https://www.tikr.com/blog/targets-q2-earnings-call-exposed-a-widening-gap-between-food-and-home-heres-the-fuller-picture. Price cut is company-announced; margin effect is inference.

findings.finding: Exit rate cooled into the holiday quarter: Placer's October visits rose +5.0% against +7.2% for calendar Q3, and BofA's November Consumer Checkpoint says October card growth 'cooled across a number of discretionary categories' (total +5.8% vs +6.2% in September), which bears on how Target frames Q4/holiday on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Holiday framing has moved this stock: 2025-11-19 (holiday outlook disappointed) -2.77%; earlier years' Q3 holiday cuts drove much larger falls.
findings.why_not_priced: Weak: both series are public. Partly visible already in the 5d -2.1% drift. If fully priced the skew would be steeper than +3.8 and the whisper would not sit 7% over consensus.
findings.independence: Placer October +5.0% (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/walmart-keeps-its-spark-as-target-hits-the-mark), a different vendor from BofA. Note October +5.0% is still positive and above Walmart's Q3 +0.7%, so this is a deceleration, not a decline; proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: More IEEPA tariff refunds may land in Q3: the CFO called the Q2 $994M a 'significant majority' of what Target expects and said more are coming, guidance excludes future refunds, and Target counts refunds inside Adjusted EPS (Q2 adj EPS $4.11 incl. $1.65), so any Q3 refund lifts the headline EPS above $2.03 mechanically; the market would likely strip it out.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, $1.65 refund in adjusted EPS: stock opened ~-4% then closed +4.28%; holders looked through the refund to the underlying beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus $2.03 and the guide exclude future refunds by construction; if a further refund were expected, EPS estimates would carry it. The path to the multiple is nil unless the money funds a raised underlying guide, so it is sized as a one-off.
findings.independence: Company release states guidance excludes future refunds (https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/08/target-corporation-reports-second-quarter-earnings); Home Depot's Q3 release on 2026-11-17 disclosed no further refund, which argues the remainder may be small or not yet received (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000354950/000035495026000184/hd_exhibit991x11012026.htm).

findings.finding: The bar is high: whisper EPS $2.17 is 7% above $2.03 consensus, shares were up ~12% from the Q2 report into 2026-11-10 and are +89% from the 52w low, and the option market pays for downside (25d skew +3.81 vol pts, implied move 8.27%), so an in-line quarter reads as a disappointment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the strongest beat of 2026 (Q1, +21% vs consensus) the stock fell 3.86%, the clearest sign this name can sell a beat when expectations are raised.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the market's own expectation, so it is priced by definition; it is filed as the bar the positive findings must clear. Short interest is 3.6% of shares (4.2 days), not crowded, so there is no squeeze offset.
findings.independence: Skew and implied move from the sealed baseline; short interest https://equibles.com/stocks/tgt/shortinterest. Shares a document with finding 2.

findings.finding: Home Depot (2026-11-17, the day before) reported Q3 comps +2.2% with ticket +3.0% and transactions -0.5% and said results 'exceeded our expectations', a modest read that the big-box consumer held up through October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no history of TGT reacting to HD's print available
findings.why_not_priced: Released this morning; partially absorbed into today's close. Home improvement has little overlap with Target's mix, so the link is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: Peer, not a counterparty; no link to Target's line beyond a common consumer. Lowe's and TJX report the same morning as Target and cannot be seen beforehand.
